rules.rule: Check for collapse following vaccination features
rules.problem: The trigger and items are correct, but it does not check the page's main discriminators: timing of collapse relative to vaccination, duration of loss of consciousness, and whether it is relieved by lying down with legs raised ('assess timing of collapse and duration of loss of consciousness'). Brief/Prolonged loss of consciousness concepts exist.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable fainting episode following vaccination
rules.problem: Discriminates only by the absence of delayed-column features plus BP>=90/60 and pulse<=120 (both inferred from the other column). The page's own criteria (sudden onset at the time of vaccination, LOC 20 s-1 min relieved by raising legs) are absent. A fainter assessed during the 'briefly low' BP is pushed into probable anaphylaxis.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable anaphylaxis after collapse following vaccination
rules.problem: Collapse + vaccination + ANY one item (e.g. cough alone, or a single BP<90/60 reading) gives probable anaphylaxis. The page describes a delayed-collapse picture (5-10 min to 1 h, LOC >1 min not relieved, BP remains low) that is not encoded. Because the two rules are exact complements on the same inputs, every assessed post-vaccination collapse gets one of the two diagnoses. Also, the red box ('Treat as anaphylaxis') has no system_priority_evaluation (Emergency, referencing active_condition Anaphylaxis), and the CPR branch (no pulse/not breathing) is not encoded.

summary: The page separates fainting from anaphylaxis mainly by timing and duration/relief of loss of consciousness, and none of these is encoded. Instead both rules split on bare Collapse + Vaccination given, with anaphylaxis triggered by any single feature (cough alone, or one transient BP<90/60 reading even though the Sudden column says BP is 'briefly low'). The red box 'Treat as anaphylaxis' also has no priority evaluation, and the fainting rule's BP>=90/60 and pulse<=120 thresholds are inferred from the opposite column rather than stated.
